alerts.title: Carbamazepine reduces DTG levels
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases dolutegravir (DTG) levels by 30-70%. The patient started carbamazepine two weeks ago and now has a detectable viral load (1,240 copies/mL) despite reported good adherence. This timing suggests a drug-drug interaction as a likely cause of virologic failure. The clinician's plan does not address this interaction.

evidence.recommended_action: Address the interaction per guidelines; consider alternative anticonvulsant (e.g., valproic acid) or adjust ART.

alerts.title: Viral load >50 requires action
alerts.message: Guidelines for patients on DTG-based ART specify that a viral load >50 copies/mL requires enhanced adherence support, addressing side-effects affecting adherence, repeating VL in 2-3 months, and considering INSTI resistance testing. The patient's VL is 1,240 copies/mL. The current plan only addresses carbamazepine toxicity, not the required virologic failure management.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide enhanced adherence support, repeat viral load in 2-3 months, and consider INSTI resistance testing.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity with hyponatremia
alerts.message: The patient has symptoms (dizziness, nystagmus, ataxia) and a level (14 mcg/mL) indicating carbamazepine toxicity. Concurrent hyponatremia (Na 128 mmol/L) is a known adverse effect of carbamazepine and can exacerbate neurological symptoms. The clinician's plan to reduce dose and repeat level is appropriate but should also address the hyponatremia.

evidence.recommended_action: Reduce carbamazepine dose, repeat level, and evaluate/manage hyponatremia.
